statement: On cvrp_dev_hetero_24 under 2000ms budget, replacing pure magnitude-based ruin scoring with a multiplicative gated rank-power score over |removal_savings|/scale (gates: route load ratio, depot prominence of the node, demand ratio, route distance share) combined with a stagnation-adaptive exponent p that increases from ~0.7 toward ~2.0 as stagnation_ratio and iter_frac grow will lower mean objective by >=0.05 versus the current 16.0293 SBS, because it keeps exploitation (high-savings removals) early and forces spatially/structurally diversified ruin sets under stagnation.
rationale: KB entry method-cvrp-m3-ruin-recreate-l3 reports the evolved hook of exactly this form (rank_power of gated removal savings with p(iter_frac, stagnation_ratio)) beat the Worst-Cost Removal L3-ctrl baseline 23.3186 vs 23.3474 on blind_120 while the deterministic Regret-2 repair and R2R acceptance are fixed; weakest dev_24 regimes (clustered spatial, eccentric depot, loose capacity) are precisely the ones stressed by load/depot/route-distance gates, so gated diversification should help there.

statement: On cvrp_dev_hetero_24 under 2000ms budget, replacing pure magnitude-based ruin scoring with a multiplicative gated rank-power score over |removal_savings|/scale (gates: route load ratio, depot prominence of the node, demand ratio, route distance share) combined with a stagnation-adaptive exponent p that increases from ~0.7 toward ~2.0 as stagnation_ratio and iter_frac grow will lower mean objective by >=0.05 versus the current 16.0293 SBS, because it keeps exploitation (high-savings removals) early and forces spatially/structurally diversified ruin sets under stagnation.
rationale: Round-5 evolved hook implemented the predicted gated multiplicative rank-power form (bounded tanh-style savings term + load/utilization slack + eccentricity gates + stagnation/iter-driven shaping) but scored mean 16.0439 on dev_24 (24/24 feasible, 173.6 ms mean), i.e. +0.0147 vs the 16.0293 SBS (session_r0002) and +0.0134 vs round-4 (16.0305). It ranked below all four archived solvers. Interpretation: at the 2000 ms budget the LNS skeleton already reaches its stagnation plateau, so the added load/depot/demand/route-distance gates mostly reduce exploitation of high-savings removals and do not buy the diversification benefit observed for the analogous rule in the KB's 500 ms blind_120 setting (23.3186 vs 23.3474). Simple magnitude/worst-cost-based ruin scoring is therefore preferable at this budget.

rationale: Superseded by a sharper successor claim for round 6: at the 2000 ms budget on dev_24 the LNS plateau is exploitation-bound, so the hook should stay near the monotone worst-cost/magnitude rule and only introduce mild, low-amplitude diversification (small exponent spread, weak gates with exponent <=0.35) rather than the strong load/depot/route-distance gating that lost 0.0147.

statement: On cvrp_dev_hetero_24 under 2000ms budget, replacing pure magnitude-based ruin scoring with a multiplicative gated rank-power score over |removal_savings|/scale (gates: route load ratio, depot prominence of the node, demand ratio, route distance share) combined with a stagnation-adaptive exponent p that increases from ~0.7 toward ~2.0 as stagnation_ratio and iter_frac grow will lower mean objective by >=0.05 versus the current 16.0293 SBS, because it keeps exploitation (high-savings removals) early and forces spatially/structurally diversified ruin sets under stagnation.
rationale: Both members of the rank-power-with-gating family are now empirically negative on cvrp_dev_hetero_24 at the 2000 ms budget. Round 5 (strong multiplicative load/depot/route-distance gates, exponent up to ~2.0) scored 16.0439 vs SBS 16.0293 (+0.0147). Round 6 tested the sharper successor (monotone magnitude backbone, robust-z + rank blend with w_rank = 0.10 -> 0.35 driven by 0.6*stagnation_ratio + 0.4*iter_frac, plus weak distance-to-seed spatial coherence, alpha <= 0.5) and scored 16.0858 vs SBS 16.0293 (+0.0565 mean tour length), i.e. low-amplitude diversification was WORSE than the strong-gating variant. So the amplitude-response hypothesis (concave, optimum near zero-to-mild amplitude) is refuted; performance is instead monotonically degraded by any reshaping of the monotone magnitude rule (portfolio ordering 16.0293 < 16.0305 < 16.0351 < 16.0439 < 16.0858 tracks added hook complexity). Direction abandoned rather than retried at other amplitudes. Note solve_ms_mean rose to 216.6 ms while all instances completed and stayed feasible (completion 1.0, valid 24/24), so the loss is score-quality-driven, not feasibility- or budget-driven.

statement: On cvrp_dev_hetero_24 under the 2000 ms budget, keep the exact monotone magnitude ruin rule (the 16.0293 SBS behavior) for the bulk of LNS iterations but splice in a schedule-switched 'route-elimination' ruin phase — pure-magnitude scoring while iter_frac < ~0.55 and stagnation_ratio < 0.6, then emphasize nodes from the lowest-load (candidate-for-elimination) routes and their spatially nearest neighbors — will lower mean objective by >=0.05 vs 16.0293. Rationale: rounds 5-7 showed that continuously reshaping the magnitude rule (any amplitude, rank blend, or gate strength) is harmful, so the magnitude backbone must be preserved verbatim; a discrete phase switch adds a genuinely different destroy mechanism (dropping near-empty routes so Regret-2 can re-pack and cut route count) that pure magnitude removal never performs, which should specifically help the weakest regimes (capacity_level=loose rel_gap -22.5%, spatial=clustered, size=100).
rationale: Archive shows seven solvers clustered in 16.029-16.136 with monotone worst-removal as the shared backbone; the abandoned h_r5 hypothesis refuted amplitude-response of gated/rank reshaping. A phase-scheduled, categorical switch to route-elimination ruin is orthogonal (changes which ruin sets are formed, not how magnitudes are scored), keeping SBS behavior as the default trajectory so downside is bounded.
